### Symbols for probability and statistics

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $(\Omega, \mathcal F, \mathbb P)$ | probability space: sample space $\Omega$, $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal F$, probability measure $\mathbb P$ |
| $\mathbb P(A)$, $\mathbb P(A \mid B)$ | probability of an event, conditional probability |
| $A^c$, $A \triangle B$ | complement $\Omega \setminus A$ of an event; symmetric difference $(A \setminus B) \cup (B \setminus A)$ |
| $2^\Omega$ | the family of all subsets of $\Omega$ |
| $\sigma(\mathcal C)$ | $\sigma$-algebra generated by a family $\mathcal C$ of subsets |
| $\mathcal B(\mathbb R^n)$ | Borel $\sigma$-algebra, generated by the boxes |
| $\limsup_n A_n$, $\liminf_n A_n$ | the events "$A_n$ for infinitely many $n$" and "$A_n$ for all but finitely many $n$" |
| $\delta_\omega$ | Dirac measure at the outcome $\omega$ |
| $X$, $Y$, $Z$ | random variables (uppercase); their values $x$, $y$, $z$ |
| $\mathbf x$ | random vector (bold lowercase), with its law stated |
| $\mathbf X = (X_1, \dots, X_n)^\top$ | random vector with components the random variables $X_i$ (bold uppercase, in the mathematics tutorial), with values $\mathbf x$ |
| $F_X(x)$ | distribution function $\mathbb P(X \leq x)$ |
| $p(x)$, $p_X(x)$ | density or mass function (of $X$) |
| $\rho$, $\rho_X$ | density (of $X$) where $p$ is a mass function or a success probability |
| $\mathbb 1_A$ | indicator of the event $A$ |
| $p(x \mid y)$, $p_{X,Y}(x, y)$ | conditional and joint density or mass function |
| $x \sim p$ | $x$ is drawn from the distribution $p$ |
| $\mathbb E[X]$, $\mathbb E_{x\sim p}[\cdot]$ | expectation (under $p$) |
| $\mathbb E[X \mid Y]$ | conditional expectation |
| $\operatorname{Var}(X)$ | variance |
| $\operatorname{Cov}(X, Y)$ | covariance |
| $\operatorname{corr}(X, Y)$ | correlation coefficient $\operatorname{Cov}(X, Y)/\sigma_X\sigma_Y$ |
| $\varphi_X(t)$, $M_X(s)$ | characteristic function $\mathbb E\,e^{itX}$, moment generating function $\mathbb E\,e^{sX}$ |
| $\Phi(z)$, $\operatorname{erf}(z)$ | standard Gaussian distribution function, error function |
| $\operatorname{Poisson}(\lambda)$ | Poisson distribution with mean $\lambda$ |
| $\mu$, $\sigma^2$, $\sigma$ | mean, variance, standard deviation |
| $\boldsymbol\mu$ | mean vector |
| $\Sigma$ | covariance matrix (plain, an exception to bold matrices) |
| $\mathcal N(\mu, \sigma^2)$, $\mathcal N(\boldsymbol\mu, \Sigma)$ | normal (Gaussian) distribution |
| $\mathcal N(\mathbf x \mid \boldsymbol\mu, \Sigma)$ | its density at $\mathbf x$ |
| $\operatorname{Bern}(p)$, $\operatorname{Bin}(n, p)$ | Bernoulli and binomial distributions with success probability $p$ |
| $\bar X_n$ | sample mean of $X_1, \dots, X_n$ |
| $S_n$, $Z_n^*$ | partial sum $X_1 + \dots + X_n$; its standardisation $(S_n - n\mu)/\sigma\sqrt n$ |
| $C_b^\infty(\mathbb R)$ | smooth functions on $\mathbb R$ all of whose derivatives are bounded (test functions of the central limit theorem) |
| $\pi_\lambda(k)$ | Poisson mass function $e^{-\lambda}\lambda^k/k!$ |
| $\hat\theta$ | estimator of a parameter $\theta$ |
| $s^2$, $\hat\sigma^2$ | sample variance with divisor $n - 1$; the variance estimate with divisor $n$ (or the one named in context) |
| $b(\theta)$, $\operatorname{MSE}(\hat\theta)$ | bias $\mathbb E\hat\theta - \theta$ and mean squared error $\mathbb E(\hat\theta - \theta)^2$ of an estimator |
| $L(\theta)$, $\ell(\theta)$ | likelihood and log-likelihood of the observed data |
| $I(\theta)$ | Fisher information of one observation, $\mathbb E_\theta[(\partial_\theta\log f(X \mid \theta))^2]$ |
| $\mathbb E_\theta$, $\mathbb P_\theta$ | expectation and probability when the parameter has the value $\theta$ |
| $z_\beta$ | Gaussian quantile, $\Phi(z_\beta) = 1 - \beta$ |
| $g_k$, $\chi^2_k$ | chi-squared density with $k$ degrees of freedom; a random variable with this density |
| $X^2$ | Pearson's chi-squared statistic $\sum_i(O_i - E_i)^2/E_i$ |
| $\hat I_N$ | Monte Carlo estimate from $N$ samples |
| $H(X)$, $H(X \mid Y)$ | entropy (differential entropy when $X$ is continuous), conditional entropy |
| $H(p, q)$ | cross-entropy |
| $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p \,\Vert\, q)$ | Kullback-Leibler divergence |
| $I(X; Y)$ | mutual information |
| $\langle A\rangle = \langle\psi, A\psi\rangle$ | quantum expectation value in the state $\psi$ |
| $\langle\cdot\rangle_\beta$ | thermal average at inverse temperature $\beta$ |

Conventions:

- $\mathbb E$ is the expectation of a random variable; $\langle\cdot\rangle$ is a quantum or thermal average.
- $\mathbb P$ is a probability; $p$ is a density or mass function.
- Entropy, cross-entropy, Kullback-Leibler divergence and mutual information use the natural logarithm (nats).
